Subject: Production: elevated 429/5xx during morning ramp

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429s and intermittent 5xx timeouts in our production integration this morning around 07:45 PST. Traffic was normal historically; we ramped a batch of inference jobs at 07:40 for a new feature rollout. The client is now getting spikes of 429 and then a short series of 500s/timeouts when retries kick in.

Attached is a small sample of request/response logs (medstream_rate_sample.log). Key points:
- Rate of 429s correlates with a batch job (roughly 2.5k reqs/min)
- We see X-Redwood-Quota headers indicating an organization limit at 60 rpm in many responses
- Our integration expects project-level capacity to be higher — we did not change our config this morning

This is affecting several customer-facing cohorts. Need immediate triage and an urgent mitigation path (throttling fallback or temporary credit/burst). Can someone confirm whether an org-tier migration or quota change happened overnight?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Integrations, MedStream Health

On Tue, Dec 15, 2026 at 08:28 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marcus/Stephanie/Aditya: can you pick this up as P1? ...

Quick summary after first-pass triage:
- No manual quota changes were recorded in the org admin logs between 00:00–08:00 PST.
- There was an automated tiering job that ran at 02:17 PST to reassign org->project tiers for cost-optimization; the job should have created a higher project-level bucket for MedStream but a fallback policy inadvertently left an org-level hard cap active.
- The X-Redwood-Quota header Sarah captured is accurate: org_limit=3600/min shows in the control plane, but project_limit=60/min is being applied in the serving path due to a mismatched policy key (we're seeing a missing project tag on some requests).
- The spike becomes a retry storm because MedStream's client retries aggressively on 429; the pattern is classic cascade failure.

Immediate mitigation options (fastest -> slower):
A) Push a temporary per-project override to raise project_limit for medstream-health project to 5000/min (requires config change but low risk) — ETA ~20m if we run the playbook.
B) Enable an emergency soft-throttle on the org level to return 429 with Retry-After and request smoothing headers (less ideal for customer UX).
C) Suggest MedStream patch client backoff (we'll provide recommended backoff window).

I'll prepare the override plan and request an ops-run. Stephanie, can you coordinate running the playbook and review the rollback steps? Aditya, please advise on customer-facing comms and whether we should offer immediate burst credits.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

- 09:25 PST: apply project_limit override to medstream-health project -> target 5,000/min
- 09:26–09:35 PST: monitor for reduction in 429 rate and cascading 5xx
- 09:40 PST: if stable, roll in a short-term credits offer for the ramp and follow up with a root-cause writeup

Customer-facing ask: could MedStream temporarily reduce client retry aggressiveness for the next 30m while we flip the override? Recommended header-based backoff: Retry-After with exponential jitter (we'll share exact guidance).

I'll provide a one-page note you can send to your teams and CSMs.

- Aditya

Subject: RE: Production: elevated 429/5xx during morning ramp — update and next steps

Sarah — quick update and next steps.

What we did:
- 09:25 PST: applied a per-project override increasing project_limit to 5,000/min for medstream-health (no code changes).
- 09:27–09:36 PST: observed 90% reduction in 429s; transient 5xx quickly subsided once client retries were smoothed.
- 10:00 PST: rolled back risky automation that caused org-level cap fallback. Engineering has a mitigation branch to ensure the tiering job tags projects consistently.

Customer impact: the integration is back to normal; we saw request throughput return to expected levels and no new escalations from your end in the following hours.

Next steps (action items):
- Marcus: complete post-mortem and push code fix for tiering job (RT-1459).
- Engineering: add a guard that prevents org-level hard caps from being applied when project tags are missing.
- CS/Finance: Kimberly/Aditya to propose a small one-time credit for the affected window and share a short FAQ for MedStream engineers on retry/backoff best practices.
- Ops: review automated tiering schedule — consider moving heavy reassignments to a low-impact maintenance window.

Thanks for your patience, Sarah. We'll follow up with a formal post-mortem and the HubSpot update.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
